name: Port-preserving homomorphisms
description: Definition 4.27: HI preserves input ports with respect to SHIS iff #IPZ2 = #IPZ1 and for each i there is HIi ∈ FNS(IiZ2, ONTO, IiZ1) with SHIS = {HIi} and PJN(IZ1,i) ∘ HI = HIi ∘ PJN(IZ2,i); dually for HO and SHOS. Port counts are encoded by a bijection σ between the port index types, so a port-preserving map may permute ports and clause (ii) says the homomorphism acts portwise through σ.

elements.text: H preserves ports with respect to a family {Hi} of surjections when PJN(·,i) ∘ H = Hi ∘ PJN(·,i) for every port i.
The family SHIS = {HIi} (resp. SHOS = {HOj}) of per-port maps.
Clause (i) for inputs: #IPZ2 = #IPZ1, encoded as a bijection between the input port index types.
Clause (i) for outputs: #OPZ2 = #OPZ1, encoded as a bijection between the output port index types.
